(f_T)^*(f_T)_*I(m)\longrightarrow I(m),

\paragraph{Step IV.}
Let $A$ be the finitely presented subscheme of $\mathcal G$ such that a map
$g:T\to\mathcal G$ factors through $A$ if and only if $H_T$ is $T$-flat
with Hilbert polynomial $\phi$; it exists by (2.3). Then we have
$H_A\in\mathbf A(A)$ and the pair $(A,H_A)$ represents $\mathbf A$.

\paragraph{Proof.}
The first assertion is clear; so, $H_A$ defines a map of functors,
\[
a:A(T)\longrightarrow\mathbf A(T).
\]
Take any $g\in A(T)$. By Step III with $G=(1\times g)^*H$, the quotients
$g^*Q$ and $(f_T)_*G(m)$ of $F_T(m)$ are equivalent. So the image
$a(g)=(1\times g)^*H$ determines the quotient of $g^*Q$, so also $g$. Thus,

Take any $G\in\mathbf A(T)$. Then, by Step II, the map
$g=\Phi(G):T\to\mathcal G$ is defined such that $g^*Q$ is equivalent to

$(1\times g)^*H$. Therefore $(1\times g)^*H$ is flat with Hilbert

\paragraph{Step V.}
We have
\[
f_*F(m)=B\otimes\Sym_{\nu+m}(E)

by the projection formula [EGA $0_{\mathrm I}$, 5.4.8] and by Serre's
explicit computation [EGA $\mathrm{III}_1$, 2.1.12]. So the Pl\"ucker
morphism is closed embedding,
\[
\mathcal G\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow
\mathbb P\!\left(\bigwedge^{\phi(m)}
  \bigl(B\otimes\Sym_{\nu+m}(E)\bigr)\right),
\qquad
Q\longmapsto\bigwedge^{\phi(m)}Q.
\]

[EGA I, 5.5.8] is satisfied [EGA $\mathrm{IV}_2$, 2.8.1].

\textit{for an embedding of $X$ into $\mathbb P(E)$, where $E$ is a locally
free $\mathcal O_S$-Module with a constant rank. Then $R$ is effective, the
quotient map $q:X\to(X/R)$ is strongly projective and faithfully flat, and
$h:(X/R)\to S$ is strongly quasi-projective.}

\paragraph{Proof. Step I.}
Set
\[
H=\coprod\Hilb^{\phi}_{(X/S)},
\]
where $\phi$ ranges over the finitely many Hilbert polynomials of $p_2$; the
$S$-scheme $H$ exists and is strongly projective by (2.8). Let $W$ denote
the universal subscheme of $X\times_S H$. Since $R$ is a flat, finitely
presented, proper subscheme of $X\times_S X$, there is a unique map
$g:X\to H$ such that the following equation holds:
\[
(1\times g)^{-1}(W)=R. \tag{2.9.1}
\]

\paragraph{Step II.}
Let $T$ be an $S$-scheme and let $x_1,x_2$ be two $T$-points of $X$. Write
$x_1\sim x_2$ whenever $(x_1,x_2)\in R(T)$ holds. Then we have
\[
x_1\sim x_2\qquad\text{if and only if}\qquad g(x_1)=g(x_2).
\]

\paragraph{Proof.}
Set $R_i=(1\times x_i)^{-1}(R)\subset X\times T$. Then
$g(x_1)=g(x_2)$ holds if and only if $R_1=R_2$ holds, so if and only if
$R_1(T')=R_2(T')$ holds for all $T$-schemes $T'$.

Clearly we have the relation,
\[
R_i(T')=\{(x,t)\in(X\times T)(T')\mid x\sim x_i(t)\}.
\]
Suppose $x_1\sim x_2$ holds. Then for $(x,t)\in R_1(T')$ we have
$x\sim x_1(t)\sim x_2(t)$. Since $R$ is transitive, we have
$(x,t)\in R_2(T')$. Thus $R_1\subset R_2$ holds. So, since $R$ is
symmetric, $R_1=R_2$ holds. Hence $g(x_1)=g(x_2)$ holds.

Suppose $g(x_1)=g(x_2)$ holds. Then $R_1(T)=R_2(T)$ holds. Since $R$ is
reflexive, we have $(x_1,\mathrm{id})\in R_1(T)$. So we have
$(x_1,\mathrm{id})\in R_2(T)$. Thus $x_1\sim x_2$ holds.

\paragraph{Step III.}
For each $S$-scheme $T$ and for $x_1,x_2\in X(T)$, we have
\[
x_1\sim x_2\qquad\text{if and only if}\qquad
(x_1,g(x_2))\in W(T).
\]
Furthermore, $\Gamma_g$ is a finitely presented, closed subscheme of $W$.

\paragraph{Proof.}
The first assertion follows immediately from Equation (2.9.1). Since $H/S$
is separated, $\Gamma_g$ is a closed subscheme of $X\times_S H$. Then,
since $R$ is reflexive, the first assertion implies the second.

The projection $p:W\to H$ is faithfully flat and quasi-compact, and
$\Gamma_g$ descends to a finitely presented subscheme $Z$ of $H$.

\paragraph{Proof.}
The projection $p$ is flat and quasi-compact by definition of
$\Hilb_{(X/S)}$. Since $R$ is reflexive and so nonempty, $p$ is surjective,
so faithfully flat. So, to descend $\Gamma_g$, it suffices to show that
$\Gamma_g\times_H W$ and $W\times_H\Gamma_g$ coincide in

and compatible with base-change, so we may assume $S$ is affine and, by
[EGA $\mathrm{IV}_3$ Sect. 8], Noetherian.

Let $\overline X$ denote the scheme-theoretic closure of $X$ in
$\mathbb P(E)$ (it exists by [EGA I, 6.10.6]), and let
$j:X\to\overline X$ be the inclusion. Let $\overline F$ denote the image of
the canonical map $B_{\overline X}(\nu)\to j_*(F)$. Since $j$ is
quasi-compact, $j_*(F)$ is quasi-coherent and $j_*(F)|X$ is equal to $F$
[EGA I, 6.9.2]. Then the image $\overline F$ of the canonical map
$B_{\overline X}(\nu)\to j_*(F)$ is locally finitely generated, so locally
finitely presented because $S$ is Noetherian. Clearly $\overline F|X$ is
equal to $F$.

Clearly $\Quot^{\phi}_{(F/X/S)}$ is a subfunctor of
$\Quot^{\phi}_{(\overline F/\overline X/S)}$. Moreover

and let $R$ be a flat, finitely presented, proper equivalence relation on

polynomials}
% [the statement continues on page-0021]

% source: Allen B. Altman and Steven L. Kleiman, "Compactifying the Picard Scheme", Adv. Math. 35 (1980)
% pdf_page: 0022
% doc_page: 72
% retrieved: 2026-06-17
% transcribed_by: codex/gpt-5.6-sol (vision, rendered at 200dpi via pdftoppm; no OCR)

% requires: amsmath

\DeclareMathOperator{\Hilb}{Hilb}

% running head: ALTMAN AND KLEIMAN / p. 72
% [continuation of Step IV in the proof of Theorem (2.9)]

$W\times_H W$ by [SGA 1, VIII, Corollary 1.9, p. 200]. For each $S$-scheme
$T$, there are formulas,
\[
(W\times_H\Gamma_g)(T)
=\{(x_1,g(x_2),x_2,g(x_2))\mid x_1\sim x_2\},
\]
\[
(\Gamma_g\times_H W)(T)
=\{(x_1,g(x_1),x_2,g(x_1))\mid x_2\sim x_1\},
\]
by Step III. Hence, $W\times_H\Gamma_g$ and $\Gamma_g\times_H W$ coincide
by Step II. Finally, since finite presentation descends down a faithfully
flat, quasi-compact map [EGA $\mathrm{IV}_2$, 2.7.1], and since $\Gamma_g$
is isomorphic to $X$, the scheme $Z$ is finitely presented.

\paragraph{Step V.}
The map $g:X\to H$ factors through $Z$, and $X\times_Z X$ is equal to $R$.
Moreover, the induced map $g:X\to Z$ is faithfully flat, finitely
presented, and strongly projective.

\paragraph{Proof.}
Since $Z$ is the result of descending $\Gamma_g$, there is a diagram with
Cartesian squares and exact rows,
\[
\begin{array}{ccccc}
\Gamma_g\times_H\Gamma_g&\rightrightarrows&\Gamma_g&\longrightarrow&Z
\\
\big\downarrow&&\big\downarrow&&\big\downarrow
\\
W\times_H W&\rightrightarrows&W&\xrightarrow{p}&H,
\end{array}
\]
% [Both squares are marked Cartesian in the printed diagram.]
where the vertical maps are embeddings. Hence $g$ factors through $Z$, and
$X\times_Z X$ is clearly equal to $R$.

The map $p:W\to H$ is finitely presented and proper by definition of
$\Hilb_{(X/S)}$. Since $W$ is a subscheme of $X\times_S H/H$ and since
$X/S$ is strongly projective, $p$ is therefore strongly projective. By
Step IV, $p$ is faithfully flat. Therefore, $g$ also has these desirable
properties.

\paragraph{Step VI.}
The theorem holds, and the induced map $g:X\to Z$ is equal to the quotient
map $X\to(X/R)$.

\paragraph{Proof.}
Since $g$ is faithfully flat (Step V) and since it is obviously
quasi-compact, it is universally an effective epimorphism [SGA I, VIII,
Corollary 5.3, p. 213]. Therefore, since $X\times_Z X$ is equal to $R$
(Step V), the map $g:X\to Z$ is a quotient map of $X$ by $R$ by Step V.
Finally, $f:(X/R)\to S$ is strongly quasi-projective because $Z$ is a
finitely presented subscheme of the strongly quasi-projective $S$-scheme
$H$.

\paragraph{(2.10) Corollary.}
\textit{Let $f:X\to S$ be a locally projective morphism of schemes, and let
$R$ be a flat, finitely presented, proper equivalence relation on $X$. Then
$R$ is effective, the quotient map is faithfully flat, finitely presented
and proper, and the quotient $(X/R)$ is locally quasi-projective over $S$.}

    12	
    13	A class over the carrier of a singleton etale cover whose two restrictions to the
    14	double overlap agree descends to the base.  The representative cover is composed with
    15	the given cover.  Its raw relative-Picard descent condition is checked after restriction
    16	to a cover of the double overlap and reflected by etale separatedness.

    34	set_option maxHeartbeats 4000000 in
    35	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
    36	theorem exists_map_eq_of_double_eq {k A : Type u} [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    37	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    38	    [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : PicEtAff C E.Carrier)
    39	    (h : mapAlg C (doubleInl E) x = mapAlg C (doubleInr E) x) :
    40	    ∃ z : PicEtAff C A, map C E.Carrier z = x := by
    41	  induction x using ind with
    42	  | _ G xi =>
    43	    obtain ⟨H, m₁, m₂, hm₁, hm₂, hm⟩ :=
    44	      exists_relPicAlgMap_eq_of_mapAlg_eq C (doubleInl E) (doubleInr E) G G xi xi h
    45	    letI : Algebra.Etale A G.Carrier :=
    46	      Algebra.Etale.comp A E.Carrier G.Carrier
    47	    letI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A G.Carrier :=
    48	      Module.FaithfullyFlat.trans A E.Carrier G.Carrier
    49	    let K : Algebra.EtaleCover A :=
    50	      Algebra.EtaleCover.of G.Carrier
    51	        PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
    52	    let e : K.Carrier ≃ₐ[A] G.Carrier :=
    53	      Algebra.EtaleCover.ofEquiv G.Carrier
    54	        PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
    55	    let j : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] K.Carrier :=
    56	      e.symm.toAlgHom.comp
    57	        ((Algebra.ofId E.Carrier G.Carrier).restrictScalars A)
    58	    let phi : E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier →ₐ[A] K.Carrier ⊗[A] K.Carrier :=
    59	      Algebra.TensorProduct.map j j
    60	    letI : Algebra (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) (K.Carrier ⊗[A] K.Carrier) :=
    61	      phi.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    62	    haveI : IsScalarTower k (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier)
    63	        (K.Carrier ⊗[A] K.Carrier) :=
    64	      .of_algebraMap_eq fun a => by
    65	        change (algebraMap k K.Carrier a) ⊗ₜ[A] 1 =
    66	          phi ((algebraMap k E.Carrier a) ⊗ₜ[A] 1)
    67	        simp [phi, j]
    68	    let L : Algebra.EtaleCover (K.Carrier ⊗[A] K.Carrier) :=
    69	      H.baseChange (K.Carrier ⊗[A] K.Carrier)
    70	    let eInv : G.Carrier →ₐ[k] K.Carrier := e.symm.toAlgHom.restrictScalars k
    71	    let xiK : relPic C (overSpec k K.Carrier) := relPicAlgMap C eInv xi
    72	    have hxiK : xiK ∈ descentClasses C K := by
    73	      rw [mem_descentClasses_iff]
    74	      apply relPicAlgMap_injective_of_etaleCover C L
    75	      let incT : K.Carrier ⊗[A] K.Carrier →ₐ[k] L.Carrier :=
    76	        (Algebra.ofId (K.Carrier ⊗[A] K.Carrier) L.Carrier).restrictScalars k
    77	      let incH : H.Carrier →ₐ[k] L.Carrier :=
    78	        (H.baseChangeInclude (K.Carrier ⊗[A] K.Carrier)).restrictScalars k
    79	      let p₁ : G.Carrier →ₐ[k] L.Carrier :=
    80	        incT.comp ((doubleInl K).comp eInv)
    81	      let p₂ : G.Carrier →ₐ[k] L.Carrier :=
    82	        incT.comp ((doubleInr K).comp eInv)
    83	      let q₁ : G.Carrier →ₐ[k] L.Carrier := incH.comp m₁
    84	      let q₂ : G.Carrier →ₐ[k] L.Carrier := incH.comp m₂
    85	      have hpq₁ : relPicAlgMap C p₁ xi = relPicAlgMap C q₁ xi := by
    86	        let beta : E.Carrier →ₐ[k] L.Carrier :=
    87	          p₁.comp ((Algebra.ofId E.Carrier G.Carrier).restrictScalars k)
    88	        letI : Algebra E.Carrier L.Carrier := beta.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    89	        haveI : IsScalarTower k E.Carrier L.Carrier :=
    90	          .of_algebraMap_eq fun a => (beta.commutes a).symm
    91	        let p₁' : G.Carrier →ₐ[E.Carrier] L.Carrier :=
    92	          { p₁.toRingHom with commutes' := fun _ => rfl }
    93	        let q₁' : G.Carrier →ₐ[E.Carrier] L.Carrier :=
    94	          { q₁.toRingHom with commutes' := fun b => by
    95	              change q₁ (algebraMap E.Carrier G.Carrier b) =
    96	                p₁ (algebraMap E.Carrier G.Carrier b)
    97	              simp [q₁, q₂, p₁, p₂, incH, incT, eInv, phi, j, hm₁,
    98	                IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply] }
    99	        exact relPicAlgMap_congr C p₁' q₁' xi.2
   100	      have hpq₂ : relPicAlgMap C p₂ xi = relPicAlgMap C q₂ xi := by
   101	        let beta : E.Carrier →ₐ[k] L.Carrier :=
   102	          p₂.comp ((Algebra.ofId E.Carrier G.Carrier).restrictScalars k)
   103	        letI : Algebra E.Carrier L.Carrier := beta.toRingHom.toAlgebra
   104	        haveI : IsScalarTower k E.Carrier L.Carrier :=
   105	          .of_algebraMap_eq fun a => (beta.commutes a).symm
   106	        let p₂' : G.Carrier →ₐ[E.Carrier] L.Carrier :=
   107	          { p₂.toRingHom with commutes' := fun _ => rfl }
   108	        let q₂' : G.Carrier →ₐ[E.Carrier] L.Carrier :=
   109	          { q₂.toRingHom with commutes' := fun b => by
   110	              change q₂ (algebraMap E.Carrier G.Carrier b) =
   111	                p₂ (algebraMap E.Carrier G.Carrier b)
   112	              simp [q₁, q₂, p₁, p₂, incH, incT, eInv, phi, j, hm₂,
   113	                IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply] }
   114	        exact relPicAlgMap_congr C p₂' q₂' xi.2
   115	      have hp₁ : relPicAlgMap C incT
   116	            (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl K) xiK) = relPicAlgMap C p₁ xi := by
   117	        rw [xiK, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp]
   118	        congr 2
   119	        ext y
   120	        rfl
   121	      have hp₂ : relPicAlgMap C incT
   122	            (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr K) xiK) = relPicAlgMap C p₂ xi := by
   123	        rw [xiK, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp]
   124	        congr 2
   125	        ext y
   126	        rfl
   127	      rw [hp₁, hp₂]
   128	      calc
   129	        relPicAlgMap C p₁ xi = relPicAlgMap C q₁ xi := hpq₁
   130	        _ = relPicAlgMap C q₂ xi := by
   131	          rw [q₁, q₂, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, hm]
   132	        _ = relPicAlgMap C p₂ xi := hpq₂.symm
   133	    let xiK' : descentClasses C K := ⟨xiK, hxiK⟩
   134	    refine ⟨mk C K xiK', ?_⟩
   135	    rw [map_mk]
   136	    let mu : E.Carrier ⊗[A] K.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier :=
   137	      Algebra.TensorProduct.lift
   138	        ((Algebra.ofId E.Carrier G.Carrier).restrictScalars A) e.toAlgHom
   139	        fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _
   140	    let mu' : E.Carrier ⊗[A] K.Carrier →ₐ[E.Carrier] G.Carrier :=
   141	      { mu.toRingHom with commutes' := fun b => by simp [mu] }
   142	    let f : (K.baseChange E.Carrier).Carrier →ₐ[E.Carrier] G.Carrier :=
   143	      mu'.comp (K.baseChangeEquiv E.Carrier).toAlgHom
   144	    refine (mk_eq_mk_iff C).mpr ⟨G, f, AlgHom.id E.Carrier G.Carrier, ?_⟩
   145	    apply Subtype.ext
   146	    rw [descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe, descentBaseChange_coe, xiK,
   147	      ← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp]
   148	    have hf : ((f.restrictScalars k).comp
   149	          ((K.baseChangeInclude E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)).comp eInv =
   150	        AlgHom.id k G.Carrier := by
   151	      ext y
   152	      simp [f, mu', mu, eInv]
   153	    have hid : (AlgHom.id E.Carrier G.Carrier).restrictScalars k =
   154	        AlgHom.id k G.Carrier := rfl
   155	    rw [hf, hid, relPicAlgMap_id]
